 Judgment

This appeal is directed against the impugned judgment and decree dated 05.08.2017 passed in O.S.No.1302/2016 by the learned III Addl.City Civil and Sessions Judge, Bengaluru, whereby the said suit filed by the respondents - plaintiffs for permanent injunction and other reliefs against the appellants - defendants in relation to the suit schedule immovable property was decreed in favour of the plaintiffs by the trial court.

sentences.text:
2. Heard learned counsel for the appellants and learned counsel for the respondents and perused the material on record.
3.
For the purpose of convenience, the parties are referred to their respective rankings in the trial court.

4. The material on record discloses that the plaintiffs instituted the aforesaid suit for permanent injunction restraining the appellants - defendants from interfering with their possession and NC:
2023:KHC:39683 enjoyment of the suit schedule property and for other reliefs.

It was contended that the respondents - plaintiffs purchased the suit schedule property vide E-Auction dated 27.11.2013 and paid the sale consideration of Rs.2,41,19,641/- to the BDA, which executed a registered sale deed and possession certificate dated 25.04.2014 in favour of the plaintiffs.
Pursuant to which, the khata was registered in their name on 23.06.2014 by the BBMP and the plaintiffs paid taxes and are in lawful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property.

It was alleged that since the appellants M Ramachandra vs Deepak Garla on 6 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15410245/
2 - defendants had attempted to interfere with the respondents - plaintiffs possession and enjoyment of the property, they instituted the aforesaid suit for permanent injunction and other reliefs.

5. The appellants - defendants filed their written statement disputing and denying the claim of the plaintiffs and contended that the 2nd defendant was the absolute owner of the suit schedule property which was situated in Sy.No.5/3B measuring 10 guntas, which she acquired by way of inheritance.

It was contended that the 2nd defendant had put up unauthorized construction over the said land and in W.P.No.970/2011 and W.P.No.47061/2011, this Court directed the BDA to consider her request for regularization of NC: 2023:KHC:39683 unauthorized construction and as such, the question of the said land being acquired by the BDA does not arise.

It was also contended that when some persons viz., Vanaja Reddy and others being friends and representatives of the plaintiffs tried to interfere with the defendants' possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property, they instituted O.S.No.1029/2016 before the trial court, which passed an order of status quo, which has been suppressed by the present plaintiffs.

Thus, the defendants sought for dismissal of the suit.
6. Based on the above pleadings, the trial court framed the following issues:-
(i) Whether the plaintiff prove their lawful possession enjoyment over the suit property as on the date of suit?
( ii) Whether the plaintiffs prove the unlawful interference?
(iii) Whether the plaintiffs prove that they are entitled fo rhte reliefs as prayed for?
(iv) What order or decree?
7. Plaintiff No.1 examined himself as PW-1 and documentary evidence at Exs.P1 to P14 were marked on behalf of the plaintiffs.
Defendants cross-examined PW-1 but did not adduce any oral or documentary evidence in support of their defence.

After hearing the parties, the trial court came to the NC: 2023:KHC:39683 conclusion that the plaintiffs had established that they were in lawful possession and enjoyment over the suit schedule property which was being interfered with by the defendants and proceeded to decree the suit in favour of the plaintiffs, aggrieved by which, the defendants - appellants are before this Court by way of the present appeal.

8. The following points arise for consideration in the present appeal:-
(i) Whether the trial court was justified in coming to the conclusion that the plaintiffs were in lawful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property?
(ii) Whether the impugned judgment and decree warrants interference in the present appeal?

Re-Point Nos. 1 and 2:-
M Ramachandra vs Deepak Garla on 6 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15410245/
3 9.

A perusal of the material on record will indicate that in order to establish that the plaintiffs are in possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property, apart from the fact that the evidence of plaintiff No.1(PW-1) has not been impeached or discredited in the cross-examination coupled with the fact that the defendants had not adduced any rebuttal defence evidence, the NC:
2023:KHC:39683 documentary evidence at Exs.P1 to P8 comprising of sale deed, possession certificate, revenue records, tax paid receipts etc., executed / issued in favour of the plaintiffs by the BDA and BBMP are sufficient to come to the conclusion that the plaintiffs were in lawful and peaceful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property.
9.1

Further, it is the specific contention of the defendants that the suit schedule property situated in Sy.No.5/3B measuring 10 guntas is owned and possessed by the defendants and that the plaintiffs do not have right over the same; however, the documentary evidence at Exs.P9 to P14 comprising of the acquisition proceedings, notifications, awards etc., clearly establish that the said land claimed by the defendants was acquired by the BDA who transferred and conveyed the suit schedule property in favour of the plaintiffs.

In fact, the award at Ex.P12 and its Annexures will clearly indicate that the 2nd defendant, wife of 1st defendant has received the entire compensation of Rs.1,44,417/- from the BDA and has voluntarily handed over possession of the entire land to the BDA on 18.07.1987 itself.

So also, Ex.P13, Notification issued under Section 16(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 also establishes that possession of the land bearing NC: 2023:KHC:39683 Sy.No.5/3B claimed by the defendants has been taken over by the BDA, who was in possession and enjoyment of the said land and had formed a layout and allotted sites including the suit schedule property in favour of the plaintiffs.

As stated earlier, apart from the fact that nothing is elicited in the cross-examination of PW-1 to discredit his testimony, the defendants have not adduced any oral and documentary evidence in support of their defence.

Under these circumstances, I am of the considered opinion that the trial court was fully justified in coming to the correct conclusion that the plaintiffs were in lawful and peaceful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property and that the defendants do not have any manner of right, title, interest or possession over the same.

9.2 The defendants - appellants have contended that no opportunity was provided to them to complete the cross- examination of PW-1 and also adduce defence evidence by the trial court and as such, it is necessary to set aside the impugned judgment and decree and remit the matter back to the trial court for reconsideration afresh.

The said contention of the defendants - appellants cannot be accepted in the light of the material on record, in particular, the order sheet maintained by the trial court which clearly indicates that sufficient opportunities were granted in favour NC:
2023:KHC:39683 of the defendants who did not avail the same nor show due diligence in defending the suit, as a result of which, they would not be entitled to any indulgence in the present appeal.

In this context, it is relevant to state that even till today, in the present appeal preferred in the year 2017, the appellants - defendants have not sought to produce the evidence which they proposed to adduce in support of their defence by filing necessary application in this regard.
Under these circumstances, I am of the view that the said contention urged by the defendants cannot be accepted.

9.3 Insofar as reliance placed by the defendants on orders passed by this Court in W.P.No.6970/2011 and W.P.No.47061/2011 are concerned, all that this Court did was grant liberty M Ramachandra vs Deepak Garla on 6 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15410245/
4 in favour of 2nd defendant herein to approach the BDA for regularization of unauthorized construction.

The orders passed by this Court in the said petitions do not indicate that the alleged right / possession of the defendants in the suit schedule property has been recognised or confirmed in any manner; on the other hand, even according to the defendants, they had put up unauthorized construction on land bearing Sy.No.5/3B and the same requires to be regularized, thereby indicating that the defendants do not have any manner of right, title, interest or NC: 2023:KHC:39683 possession over the suit schedule property, particularly when no order of regularization has been produced by the defendants - appellants in the present appeal and consequently, even this contention of the appellants cannot be accepted.

9.4 Insofar as the contention urged by the defendants as regards the interim order passed in O.S.No.1029/2016 is concerned, the said suit was not filed against the plaintiffs herein and as such,
any interim order passed therein cannot be relied upon by the defendants in support of their defence and as such, even this contention cannot be accepted.
9.5

As stated supra, the trial court has correctly and properly considered and appreciated the entire material on record and arrived at the correct conclusion that the plaintiffs are in lawful and peaceful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property and was entitled to a decree for permanent injunction.

9.6 Upon re-appreciation, re-evaluation and reconsideration of the entire material on record, I am of the view that the trial court was fully justified in decreeing the instant suit in favour of the respondents - plaintiffs against the appellants - defendants and that the impugned judgment and decree cannot be said to suffer from any illegality or infirmity nor can the same be said to be - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:39683 perverse or capricious warranting interference by this Court in the present appeal, which is devoid of merit and deserves to be dismissed.
Accordingly, point Nos. 1 and 2 are answered against the appellants.
10. In view for the foregoing reasons, appeal is hereby dismissed.
